changes.ink: The page contains the drawn contours, free ends, arrows, numbered regions, lettered points and small filled or hollow marks inventoried below. H prose descriptions are not copied as source text.

changes.place: Upper polygon, pale contour to its right
changes.ink: The crop shows pale tonal variation to the right of the dark polygon, but I cannot trace a continuous front-side contour matching the large closed sweep supplied by C. It is omitted as unsupported, without calling it illegible or asserting a reverse-side origin.

changes.place: Upper polygon, edge loops, free stroke and arrow tips
changes.c: No small loop beyond apex; single descending diagonal; no separate outer-right stroke or lower edge arrow tips
changes.ink: Immediately beyond the filled apex a small loop returns to the upper edge. A narrow doubled stretch lies on the descending interior diagonal. A separate thin stroke runs outside the right side, and short converging heads occur on the right and lower edge strokes.

changes.place: Upper cut sphere, faint ellipse above right side
changes.ink: No coherent narrow ellipse is traceable at the place where C supplies one. The pale area is not promoted into a source contour.

changes.c: Top small ellipse with solid centre; bottom circular point
changes.ink: The heavy upper mark encloses two small white openings and a short right-hand hook. The lower mark is a small upright protrusion from the boundary, rather than a detached circular point.

changes.c: One narrow ellipse and straight arrow
changes.ink: Several looped contours overlap along the median: a narrow upper loop, a broader lower loop and a further narrow loop below it. A converging arrowhead lies beside the upper portion of the broader loop. The numbered labels remain separate from these contours where the ink permits.

A short upright residual stroke is visible in the crowded lower-left wedge, but it merges into the dark bordering strokes. It cannot be established as an independent numeral1. C doubt is retained and is not completed from the surrounding number sequence.
The long upright has short parallel retraced portions near its upper and lower ends. No label or numeral accompanies it.

changes.place: Upper handle, opening continuations, diameters and small hole
changes.c: Outer boundary ends before right opening; solid opening diameters; only one filled spot at upper hole
changes.h: Handle with hole and dashed paths
changes.ink: The outer boundary continues into the right terminal opening. The short diameters across the two terminal openings are visibly broken. Three dark spots lie along the upper small-hole cross stroke, and that hole has a small gap at its upper edge.
Short converging tips occur on the left outer arc and on the right outer and inner arcs; they point upward along the respective curves.

changes.place: Middle ring, dashed-path arrows, contacts and partial outlines
changes.c: Regular closed ellipses; dashed paths without arrow tips
changes.ink: The dashed longitudinal path bears a downward/rightward tip on the left lower portion, a downward tip on the right and a leftward tip near the upper right. The lower meridian has an upward tip. Small filled contacts and partial retraced arcs are retained without making every retrace into a separate closed ring.

The b has an upright stem and lower bowl. The smaller subscript has a closed oval and short exit stroke, supporting a rather than the open c alternative. The crossing diagonal partly obscures the label, so confidence is medium.

changes.place: Labelled triangle, right descending central stroke
changes.c: Plain curve from a to lower-right corner
changes.ink: The right central descending stroke has a short converging tip near its lower portion. A short downward head is included along the same curve, without adding another edge.

changes.c: Closed outer boundary and closed upper meridian loop
changes.ink: There is a genuine blank gap on the left outer boundary. The upper meridian has two separately ending right-facing tips; they do not join into the closed loop in C. The inner horizontal stroke also ends freely.

changes.place: Lower-middle ring, circled point and path directions
changes.c: Empty upper-right circle; missing inner-loop arrow; solid right lower meridian
changes.ink: The small upper-right oval encloses a solid dot. A short inner-loop arrow points down-left, while the rim arrow approaches the circled mark from above. The right side of the lower meridian is broken, and the low contact is filled.

changes.place: Lower handle, terminal strokes and contours
changes.c: Long dashed line through left terminal ellipse; simplified terminal marks
changes.ink: The left terminal ellipse has a cluster of short broken strokes concentrated near its bottom and a small downward tip there; it does not show C continuous series of dashes through its whole height. The right terminal opening has a longer broken diameter. The open ends, filled contacts and directions are reproduced schematically from their positions.
The round stroke ends in two converging short strokes forming an arrowhead. This is the same visible loop-and-head form as the upper polygon orientation sign, not an alphabetic or numeric5.
The descending diagonal turns through a rounded corner into a short leftward hook. There is no second arm for a symmetric arrowhead.

The word has a tall initial stroke, a compressed low connected run and a large descending loop later in the word. The slant and joined strokes leave the full letter sequence insecure; neither the shared witness reading nor the geometric subject settles it.
The three counts occupy separate slanted lines. No commas are visible after the first two nouns; H inline commas are not transferred to the transcription.
The first digit has a curved upper stroke, descending diagonal and curved lower foot; the second has a top bar, descending stem and crossbar. The reading is27.

No such heading occurs on the current image. H own attached note explicitly assigns it to the next leaf in its pagination. It is a wrong-page inclusion in this packet, not omitted source text on scan028.

decisions.ink: The residual upright in the lower-left wedge touches or merges with the bordering dark strokes. It cannot securely be isolated as a free numeral, and the expected sequence is not evidence.
The smaller subscript has a closed oval and short exit stroke rather than an open crescent. The preceding letter has b stem and bowl; the crossing diagonal partially overlaps it.

notes.text: Landscape manuscript drawing sheet in his hand. All nine principal drawings, the separate cross, the crossing diagonal, the three-line count text and marginal27 are retained. No insertion, cancelled textual passage, typescript or letter was identified on this scan.

The large gray sweep to the right of the upper polygon and the narrow gray ellipse above the cut sphere supplied by C are omitted because no coherent matching source contour can be traced confidently. Their origin is not asserted to be bleed-through; neither area is labelled illegible.
The interior1 remains doubtful. Clear surrounding labels are2,3,4,5,6 and the six primed numbers, with a separate6 below. The unconfirmed1 is not supplied from numerical order.
The first two lines read4 sommets and6 arêtes. The final noun remains hexagones|triangles, with hexagones first. No Euler-characteristic or topological check has been used to decide it.
H terminal M_{0,5} section is absent on this image; H accompanying note assigns it to its next leaf. It is excluded from scan028. No other scan was inspected to make that decision.

Drawings are schematic TikZ reproductions. Open ends, one-sided hooks, circled filled points, partial retracing, broken strokes and identifiable arrow directions are preserved. Small crowded medial loops and overwritten-looking line contacts are not promoted into textual deletions or extra labelled objects.
27 is treated as foliation in another unnamed hand. No explicit date was read on this page.
No mathematical claim was proved or numerically checked during this page reading. Reading source counts and arrowheads is paleographical inspection, so the CHECK_EVENTS list is empty.
